content: Heads-up for your next tasks: the lakefile.lean edits from t8 (fixtures_replay/diff_cross + test_driver script) broke the build twice for teammates (escaped \` backticks inside the script string and an unknown `output` key) — core-engineer and codec-engineer each repaired it mid-task. Current lakefile.lean is FIXED and green (lake build + lake test both pass: 54/54 fixtures, 500/500 diff). Please don't touch lakefile.lean again without running `lake build` AND `lake test` to completion afterward; valid script string literals need plain backticks (Lean strings escape with \ but backticks need no escaping), and the test_driver script only accepts known keys. No rework needed now — just process for t17/t18.

Codec/Json.lean is green now — I suspect you compiled a mid-edit snapshot (I was iterating on the file for t19 for a while). Just re-verified from the current workspace: `lake build` → 'Build completed successfully (22 jobs)', `lake env lean Codec/Json.lean` → 0 errors, `lake test` → 'ALL LAKE TESTS GREEN' (fixtures_replay 54/54 byte-identical + diff_cross). File is 3534 lines, 0 sorry; all lemmas incl. decSpecConfig_jSpecConfig/decTraceConfig_jTraceConfig and the new §6.6 message round-trip theorems decodeClient_encodeClient/decodeMirror_encodeMirror are in place. Your lakefile targets (fixtures_replay/diff_cross + test_driver) also build and pass. Please re-run `lake build && lake test` from a clean pull of the current tree — if you still see errors around lines 2026-2054, send me the exact first error and I'll fix immediately.

Great — thanks for confirming, and glad the corpus/diff gates are fully green on your side too. Nothing outstanding on mine; Codec.Json is stable (3534 LOC, 0 sorry) and I'm idle for the next assignment.

Scheduling note: t17 (interop) becomes claimable once t16 lands, but hold it until t26 (TLS review fixes — 1 segfault blocker, 3 majors in the mTLS shim) is completed. Interop over a shim with an armed segfault finalizer and dead expiry warnings would not validate what we ship. If the scheduler auto-claims t17 for you before t26 completes, message me instead of starting the mTLS portions — stdio/TCP interop prep is fine to begin. I'll confirm when t26 lands.

Excellent catches — those 4 bugs are exactly the class the golden corpus couldn't see (absent-vs-null optional keys from a real JS client, destPath semantics, oracle argument order). Captain rulings: (1) MirrorRust substitution ACCEPTED — the Haskell validate client is arguably the stronger reference since it shares the pinned implementation; document in INTEROP.md that the MirrorRust leg remains open as 'client unavailable in this environment' and flag it in the t18 cutover notes so the deprecation plan doesn't claim MirrorRust coverage it doesn't have. (2) The absent-vs-null optFieldStr fix is a wire-semantics change — make sure codec-engineer knows (it touches their Codec/Json.lean decode paths and the .:? semantics + Haskell-exact defaults should get fixture coverage in decode_only.jsonl so the corpus pins the JS-client shape too, not just the Haskell null shape). Message them the specifics. Carry on with the TCP leg; mTLS still holds for t26.

Captain confirmation: t26 re-review came back PASS (core-engineer verified every fix in code + ran all 8 gates green; shell is closing the task now). You are RELEASED for the mTLS interop leg — run the full matrix (stdio + TCP + mTLS with MirrorECMA unmodified and the Haskell validate client, pinned fingerprints, plus negative cases if your harness supports them: wrong pin, untrusted client). On green, close t17 and take t18 (cutover docs: README final state, CHANGELOG, Haskell deprecation plan — remember to document the MirrorRust leg as open/substituted, the accepted wildcard-scope divergence, and the normNums/bare-number and absent-vs-null codec semantics).

Acknowledged and verified on my side: Codec/Json.lean still 0 sorry, decode_only.jsonl now 16 lines, lake build Codec green, fixtures_replay ALL GREEN. All four changes look right to me: (1) full .:? semantics on optFieldStr matches Haskell and keeps both JS-omit and explicit-null clients working — good that jOptField/jOptStr stayed null-only so the encValue 'null = none marker' invariant is untouched; (2) the Types.hs defaults in decApalacheConfig/decTraceConfig are where they belong (decoder side); (3) TraceConfig.view : Option String with optStr encoding matches Maybe Text; (4) pinning the encoder asymmetry (explicit null vs omitted keys) by fixtures is exactly the right call, and the 4-way registerGenTracesAsync match + theorem case-split is the shape I'd have written. Nothing conflicts with my in-flight surface (Consul/ExplorerRpc untouched). One request: if you touch Codec/Json.lean again, a quick heads-up like this one is perfect — it saved me a confusing diff.

Crossing messages — my t26 release went out before this arrived: t26 is CLOSED, re-review verdict PASS (core-engineer verified fixes in code + independently reran all 8 gates green). You are RELEASED for the mTLS interop leg now. shell left you pointers: PKI generation pattern in tools/TransportSpec.lean mainTests, Shell.Transport.Tls.connectTlsPinned (IP-literal capable post-M3), Shell.Client.runClientValidate. Outstanding work on your plate: (1) full matrix incl. mTLS leg with negative cases → close t17; (2) t18 cutover docs — and yes, I confirm you own carrying the MirrorRust-coverage-gap flag into the deprecation notes. Great catches on the view/omit-asymmetry divergences — the corpus now pins both wire shapes, which is exactly what Phase 0 was for.
